text: System Rule & Benchmark: Core Dispatch Rule (AI Predictive Trigger): Every 15 minutes the controller checks the renewable forecast (PV + wind) for 30 minutes ahead. Whenever Load minus 95% of forecasted renewable power exceeds 2 kW, the diesel generator is ordered to start early so it is online before the drop hits.

System Rule & Benchmark: Start-Up Delay & Unserved Load Rule: The diesel generator requires 30 minutes between receiving a start order and synchronizing online. Under Reactive (No-AI) control, the diesel starts only after a deficit already occurs, causing unserved load during that 30-minute warm-up window.

System Rule & Benchmark: Minimum Run Time & Shutdown Rule: Once started, the diesel runs for at least 1 hour to prevent damaging start-stop cycling. It shuts down only after the minimum run time is met and the forecast shows no shortfall.
System Rule & Benchmark: Diesel Rating & Minimum Loading Rule: The diesel generator is rated at 100 kW and operates at a minimum load of 30% (30 kW) whenever online to avoid wet-stacking.

System Rule & Benchmark: Forecasting & Alert Architecture: Hourly PV power is predicted via Random Forest / Gradient Boosting using weather lags and cyclical hour features, while SMOTE balances rare deficit-alert events (22 alerts in NASA Bengaluru data at 2 kW threshold, 11 alerts in synthetic data at 10 kW threshold) so the classifier catches impending renewable drops.

System Rule & Benchmark: Real Weather (NASA POWER Bengaluru) vs. Synthetic Results: Across 1,440 hourly records for Bengaluru, India, AI predictive dispatch cut unserved energy by 61.5% (from 136.12 kWh reactive down to 52.40 kWh AI) on NASA weather data, and by 62.1% (from 286.42 kWh down to 108.44 kWh) on synthetic data, trading slightly higher diesel fuel use for reliability.
System Rule & Benchmark: Fuel & CO2 Emissions Model: Diesel fuel consumption (L/h) = 0.246 * 100 kW + 0.08415 * Output_kW, and CO2 emissions equal 2.68 kg per litre of fuel burned.
